transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I feel like I’m constantly going from one thing to the next. Like I can’t really just sit still or idle, even when I should be able to. And with the new setup at work, it’s been harder to cover that up or work around it.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Yeah, sometimes. At work especially, if I hear a coworker working through a customer issue, I’ll just jump in with the answer before they’re done talking or before anyone’s asked me. I don’t mean to be rude, it just comes out.
Do you often find it hard to focus on one task for a long time?

Yeah, I do. Like in longer coaching meetings, or if I’m reading a new procedure at work, I’ll start off okay. But after a few minutes I’ll realize my eyes have been moving over the page or I’ve been sitting there listening, but I didn’t really take in what was said.
Do you feel like your difficulty sitting still, acting on impulse, or having trouble focusing is causing problems for you in your daily life?

Yes. It’s starting to cause problems at work. It’s come up in my reviews now—my supervisors have pointed out unfinished tickets and mistakes that slow the team down. I am trying hard, and I usually do fine with customers, but those things are still showing up.
Have you always had trouble sitting still or paying attention, even when you were a kid?

Yeah, looking back, I think it’s been there a long time. Even in grade school, teachers would write things like I was bright but careless, or that I talked out of turn. I remember getting reminded a lot to stay on my work. So it’s not just something that started with this job.
Do you often fidget or feel restless when you're sitting or standing still?

Yeah, I do. Even if I’m trying to sit there and look calm, my foot will be bouncing under the desk, or I’ll be clicking a pen in a meeting without realizing I’m doing it. It’s not usually a big thing, but it happens a lot.
Did you have difficulty with organization and time management as a kid?

I’m not really sure. I don’t remember a lot of specific problems with organizing things or managing time as a kid. I know teachers had to remind me sometimes, but as far as being disorganized or always late, I can’t really say for sure.
As a kid, did you often run, climb, or play more than other kids when you were supposed to be playing quietly?

I don’t remember a lot about running or climbing more than other kids, honestly. What I do notice, even now, is quiet activities don’t last long for me. Like if I’m reading at home or watching a movie with my wife, I’ll start shifting around, making comments, or getting up for something before too long.
Are your symptoms causing problems in your relationships with family or friends?

I’m not really sure it’s causing major problems there. I mean, I don’t think my family or friends would say it’s ruining anything. Maybe it annoys people sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it being a big relationship issue.
Have you noticed your wife or anyone else in your personal life commenting on your behavior or habits?

Yeah, mostly my wife notices it. Like if we’re watching a movie, I’ll start shifting around or making little comments, or I’ll get up to do something instead of just sitting through it. Same thing with reading at home — it’s supposed to be relaxing, but I don’t usually stay with it very long.
Did you have any of these symptoms, like fidgeting or acting on impulse, when you were very young, like in preschool?

Preschool I’m not really sure — I don’t remember that far back very well. But I do know it was around when I was in grade school. Teachers would write things like I was bright but careless, or that I talked out of turn and needed reminders to stay with my work. So it wasn’t just something that started recently.
Did your parents or any other family members mention that you had trouble sitting still or paying attention when you were little?

I don’t remember my parents saying a lot specifically, but looking back, it was definitely around when I was in grade school. Teachers would write that I was bright but careless, that I talked out of turn, and that I needed reminders to stay with my work. So it was there long before this job change.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention when you're doing things you enjoy or find interesting?

Yeah, even then sometimes. If it’s something I’m interested in, I can start off okay, but if it goes on for a while—like a longer coaching meeting or reading through a new procedure—I’ll realize my eyes are still moving over the words, but I didn’t really absorb it. Same with someone talking for a few minutes; I’ll come back and realize I missed part of what was said.
Have you noticed your symptoms affecting how you interact with friends or causing them to react differently to you?

Yeah, I think so, more at work than with friends. I don’t mean to be rude, but if I hear coworkers talking through a customer problem, I’ll sometimes jump in with the answer before they’ve finished, or before anyone asked me. I can tell it annoys people sometimes, like I’m butting in.
Have you experienced these symptoms at home, at work, or in other settings outside of work?

Yes, it’s definitely not just at work. At home, even quiet things that are supposed to be relaxing can be hard for me. Like if I’m reading, I don’t stay with it long before I’m shifting around. Or sitting through a movie with my wife, I’ll start making comments or get up to do something. It’s not terrible, but it happens enough that I notice it.
Have you ever lost a friend or had a friendship end because of your behavior or habits?
No, I don’t think I’ve lost a friend over it. I mean, I’m sure I’ve irritated people here and there, but I can’t point to a friendship ending because of how I act or my habits.
Have you ever felt like your behavior or habits have strained your relationship with your wife?

Yeah, a little. Nothing major, but with my wife it can be annoying for her. Like if we’re trying to watch a movie, I’ll start shifting around, making comments, or I’ll get up to do something instead of just sitting there. Same with reading at home — I don’t stay settled very long. I think it can wear on her sometimes.
Have you experienced these symptoms consistently across different settings, such as at home, at work, and in social situations, for most of your life?

Yeah, looking back, it’s been there a long time, not just since this job or anything. Even in grade school, teachers would say I was bright but careless, or that I talked out of turn and needed reminders to stay on my work. So I guess it has shown up in different parts of my life for a long time.
Have you ever felt like your symptoms have significantly strained or damaged a close relationship?

Significantly damaged, no, I wouldn’t say that. But it has strained things a bit with my wife. Like quiet things that are supposed to be relaxing — reading at home or watching a movie together — I don’t last very long before I’m shifting around, making comments, or getting up to do something. I can tell that gets annoying for her sometimes.
Have you ever had difficulty maintaining a romantic relationship because of your symptoms?

Not really in the sense of losing a relationship over it. My wife and I are okay. The bigger place it’s been showing up lately is work — in my reviews, supervisors have pointed out unfinished tickets and mistakes that slow the team down. I’m trying hard, and I usually get along fine with customers, but that part has been an issue.
